Source: National Cultural Heritage Administration (国家文物局, NCHA)
Coverage (layers, regions): Institutional engagement (aid restoration, joint archaeology, Asian Cultural Heritage Protection Action, ACHA); UNESCO and nominations (China's own and transnational). Global, with focus on Asia, Silk Roads, Africa.
How systematic: Semi-structured. No dedicated international column: overseas items are scattered across 文物要闻, 工作动态 and 政务公开. Article URLs are dated (/art/YYYY/M/D/).
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Scraping via dated article URLs. Site search (/jsearch/) did not respond to plain URL queries; needs browser automation. Loads from outside China.
Historical versions: Yes: archive back to at least 2014; five-year plans 2017, 2021, 2026 form a dated series.
Framing notes: Official policy language: 文明交流互鉴, 一带一路, 服务国家外交大局, 全球文明倡议, 中国智慧和方案.
Reliability: High for what China says and does; not neutral.

Source: NCHA five-year plans (十三五 2017, 十四五 2021, 十五五 2026)
Coverage (layers, regions): All four layers at policy level: named aid projects, joint nominations (Maritime Silk Road, Tea Road), joint archaeology target regions.
How systematic: Highly systematic: same document type every five years, comparable sections.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Manual (3 documents). 14th plan is hosted on ndrc.gov.cn.
Historical versions: Yes: 2017, 2021, 2026. Best single source for tracking framing change (Phase 5).
Framing notes: 2017: Maritime Silk Road nomination as domestic work. 2026: 'transnational joint nomination' preparatory work; 'serve the overall diplomatic agenda'.

Source: Ministry of Culture and Tourism (文化和旅游部, MCT)
Coverage (layers, regions): Intangible heritage policy and UNESCO ICH nominations (incl. joint China-Malaysia element); cultural exchange; China Cultural Centres abroad.
How systematic: Semi-structured news and policy columns; plans issued as PDF attachments.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Scraping of news pages; PDFs for plans (ICH 15th five-year plan issued 2026-09-21 as PDF, not yet read).
Historical versions: Yes: news archive; five-year ICH plans.

Source: China Intangible Cultural Heritage Network (中国非物质文化遗产网, ihchina.cn)
Owner type: Chinese government-affiliated (run by China ICH Protection Center under MCT)
Coverage (layers, regions): National ICH list: 3,610 items; 45 UNESCO-inscribed items. Descriptions often mention overseas Chinese, Southeast Asia, Taiwan.
How systematic: Highly structured: item ID, number (e.g. Ⅹ-85), title, category, new/extension, year and batch, province/city code, description.
Historical versions: Partial: listing year and batch per item; descriptions not dated.
Framing notes: Diaspora framing: Nanyin as 'spiritual bond' for overseas compatriots and Taiwan compatriots; Mazu spread 'following the footsteps of overseas Chinese'. National title 闽台送王船 (Fujian-Taiwan) vs UNESCO's China + Malaysia.

Source: Chinese embassy websites (e.g. Cambodia, Malaysia, Kenya, Uzbekistan)
Coverage (layers, regions): Institutional engagement and narrative layers per host country: heritage exhibitions, restoration projects, ambassador essays on shared history, overseas-Chinese affairs (领侨动态).
How systematic: Semi-structured. Common Foreign Ministry template on every *.china-embassy.gov.cn site; dated URLs (/column/YYYYMM/tYYYYMMDD_id.htm). Some list pages render by script.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Scraping by dated URL pattern; search runs through a central Foreign Ministry engine (fmprc.gov.cn/irs-c-web/search.shtml) filterable by site. Some old URLs (pre-2013) now redirect to the homepage: use the Wayback Machine.
Historical versions: Yes: Kenya archive back to 2005, Malaysia to 2012 in samples.
Framing notes: Heavy framing: 'civilisations learning from each other' (互学互鉴), Zheng He as friendship, 'Silk Road spirit', 'community with a shared future'.
Reliability: High for official narrative; low for facts on sites.

Source: Chinese Academy of Cultural Heritage (中国文化遗产研究院, CACH)
Coverage (layers, regions): Institutional engagement: lead agency for aid restoration (Angkor Chau Say Tevoda 1998, Ta Keo 2010, Royal Palace 2018).
How systematic: Own site not yet tested; project information mostly via NCHA and media interviews.
Framing notes: Frames Angkor work as China being among the earliest participants in UNESCO's international safeguarding campaign.

Source: CASS Institute of Archaeology (中国社会科学院考古研究所) and cssn.cn
Coverage (layers, regions): Joint archaeology abroad: Uzbekistan (2012-), Honduras Copan (2015-), Egypt Monthu Temple (2018-), Romania (2019-), Greece (2026). 2026 catalogue 《大道东风》 of overseas results.
How systematic: Semi-structured: news and features on cssn.cn; excavation reports as books.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Scraping of cssn.cn articles; reports need library access.
Framing notes: 'Independent knowledge system' (自主知识体系); from 'archaeological power' to 'archaeological strength'.

Source: Provincial and university archaeology teams (e.g. Shaanxi Institute of Archaeology, Northwest University, Peking University)
Coverage (layers, regions): Joint archaeology in Central Asia (Kyrgyzstan Red River site, Shaanxi) and East Africa (Kenya Lamu/Malindi, Peking University, c. 2010-2013).
How systematic: Scattered: press releases, university news, academic papers.
Framing notes: Kenya work framed around Zheng He's voyages and 'rewriting East African coast history'.

Source: Alliance for Cultural Heritage in Asia (亚洲文化遗产保护联盟, ACHA)
Coverage (layers, regions): Institutional engagement across Asia: 10 founding states (China, Armenia, Cambodia, DPRK, Iran, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Syria, UAE, Yemen); roadmap includes Silk Roads archaeology, World Heritage nominations, restoration in Türkiye and Syria. NCHA's 2026 plan adds an 'Asian cultural heritage database'.
How systematic: No dedicated website found; information via NCHA and state media.

Source: Belt and Road portal (中国一带一路网, yidaiyilu.gov.cn)
Coverage (layers, regions): Aggregates heritage and archaeology news framed under Belt and Road.
Framing notes: Belt and Road framing by definition.

Source: Overseas-Chinese institutions (Overseas Chinese History Museum of China; Jinan University Academy of Overseas Chinese Studies; China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese)
Owner type: Chinese state museum / university / mass organisation
Coverage (layers, regions): Historical Chinese presence layer: diaspora history, qiaopi, associations, temples abroad.
How systematic: Weakly structured online. Jinan has a documentation centre and journals (《东南亚研究》, 《海外华人研究》) but no open database found.

Coverage (layers, regions): Chinese academic writing on overseas heritage, Maritime Silk Road, joint archaeology; useful for dating when terms emerge.
How systematic: Highly structured bibliographic records with dates.
Framing notes: Good for counting term frequency over time (e.g. 海上丝绸之路 since the 1980s).
Reliability: High as a record of discourse.
